O Playwright MCP dá um navegador ao seu: Playwright MCP gives your coding agent a browser. It doesn't send a screenshot: it sends the accessibility snapshot, with a reference (ref) on each control, and the agent acts through those refs. In this lesson a script makes exactly the calls the agent would make, without a model, and then you connect the server to Claude Code or Codex.

The agent opens the URL. Playwright MCP 0.0.83 replies with the URL, the title, how many errors are in the console and, if the page registered WebMCP tools, how many there are (lesson 4).
browser_snapshot devolve a árvore de ace: browser_snapshot returns the accessibility tree in YAML: role, name and one ref per element, like textbox "Seu nome" [ref=e13]. It's the same format course 0 printed, now with refs.
The model reads the snapshot and picks the ref. In the dry run, ver-como-agente.mjs does the picking, looking for role and name. If a control has no name, neither one can find it reliably.
browser_type, browser_select_option e br: browser_type, browser_select_option and browser_click receive target (the ref) and element (a text description, used to ask for permission). Then a new snapshot shows the result.
A ref vale para aquele snapshot. Mudou a: A ref is valid for that snapshot only. If the page changed, take another.
